result.title: The Between-Round Decision in Autonomous Research: An LLM Controller That Reads the Whole Trajectory
result.summary: Executing an idea often changes how promising it looks, so the next step in autonomous research should rest on results, not on proposals. After each round of experiments, the system must decide whether to refine the best solution or start a new direction, which solution to build from, and what goal to set. We call this the between-round decision. Existing systems wrap it in machinery such as rules, scores, search trees, and schedules; where an LLM makes it, what the LLM needs to read is left open. We ask whether an LLM can make this decision from accumulated evidence, without a search structure around it, and how much of that evidence it needs to read. We present BRED (Between-Round Evidence-based Decision), an LLM-based controller that maintains the best verified solution so far (the Champion) and a log of past rounds, and makes one decision per round. On three widely used research-agent benchmark tasks, BRED improves on the task baselines by 4.80% in MAE on ETTh1 (to 0.4172) and by 3.44 and 3.43 points of accuracy on SST-2 (to 95.07%) and CIFAR-100 (to 84.63%), ahead of the published results. When the controller does not read the accumulated evidence, the same loop gains less: with no history it reaches 0.4299 on ETTh1 and 83.71% on CIFAR-100, whereas the full controller's MAE is 2.95% lower and its accuracy 0.92 points higher. On a new task, speech-based depression detection under a leakage-free protocol, it reaches a macro-F1 of 0.6164 on seeds held out from selection, 5.5 points above its baseline and 4.0 above the strongest published system. Code is available at https://github.com/learninginvision/BRED.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 BRED，一个基于 LLM 的控制器：每轮实验后读取当前最优解（Champion）与历史轮次日志，在无搜索结构的情况下决定是继续精修、换方向、以哪个解为基础以及设什么目标，并对比不读累积历史时的增益，在多个研究型 agent 基准及语音抑郁检测任务上评测。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「需要读取多少累积证据、以压缩状态而非外部搜索结构支撑逐轮决策」的设计与消融，可供核查 LVR 中证据保留、状态更新与停止/取舍决策的对照线索；但任务并非视觉多模态，迁移性需进一步判断。
